key_insight: Compared with BETS, relaxed λ-(STF)₂GaCl₄ has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining substantial dimerization, and unrelaxed-structure Wannier models reveal selectively weakened electronic connectivity.
engineering_relevance: The results inform low-energy model construction for molecular conductors by showing how donor substitution and structural relaxation affect electronic coupling.
method: Compute near-Fermi electronic structures using DFT.
Compare DFT-selected and XRD-refined STF structures before and after fixed-lattice relaxation.
Construct two maximally localized Wannier functions per selected unrelaxed structure to extract transfer integrals.
evidence_signal: Initially different STF electronic structures become similar after relaxation; unrelaxed-structure Wannier models yield total spreads of 36.708 Å² for BETS and 37.578 Å² for STF, with t_d1 decreasing from 51 to 6.5 meV.
watch_item: Transfer integrals were extracted from selected unrelaxed structures, so their quantitative applicability to relaxed structures remains to be checked.
paper_title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
